topic: Geometric Mean and the AM-GM Inequality
title: Which Average Wins? AM-GM Inequality Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Take 4 and 9. Add and halve: 6.5. Multiply and take the square root: 6. Try any pair of positive numbers and the first answer always wins, or ties. Luck, or a rule? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 8, Sequences and Series) we meet the geometric mean and prove the AM-GM inequality.

You will see the geometric mean as the side of a square with the same area as a rectangle, insert geometric means between two numbers (NCERT's 1 and 256), and watch a live race where the total stays at 10 while G climbs towards A and meets it only when the two numbers are equal. Then the four-step proof that A - G = (root a - root b)^2 / 2 is never negative, the NCERT worked example (A.M. 10 and G.M. 8), the exam trap with negative numbers, an original JEE Main pattern question on a smallest value, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
